- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underperforms when sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33); apply smoothing filter or use sentiment-weighted average of 5-day window.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33), model tends to lag; add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
- If true outcome is >10% above model, sentiment was likely bullish; future forecasts should be conservative unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If true outcome is <10% below model, sentiment was likely bearish; future forecasts should be cautious, especially if sentiment remains negative.
